content:
Everyone said we needed a complete rewrite before adding AI. We proved them wrong.

6 min read
Just now

--

Our enterprise application had survived Windows Server migrations, cloud migrations, framework upgrades, and multiple CTOs.
It had been running the business for over 15 years.
Millions of transactions.
Hundreds of thousands of lines of C#.
Thousands of business rules accumulated over more than a decade.
It wasn’t built with AI in mind. In fact, it was built years before anyone had heard the term “LLM.”
Then one day leadership asked a question that made every architect in the room nervous.
“Can we add AI by next quarter?”
Not after migrating to .NET 10.
Not after rewriting everything into microservices.
Not after spending two years modernizing the platform.
They wanted AI now.
For a few days, our team debated the obvious solution: rewrite the application.
Fortunately, we didn’t.
Looking back, that decision saved us months of work, millions of dollars in engineering effort, and allowed us to deliver business value far sooner than anyone expected.
